text:
lina_cs: Quick handback checklist for Acme trial tomorrow — short customer-facing run for caching / batching / streaming. Draft below, please skim and flag gaps.

lina_cs: RUNBOOK DRAFT (TL;DR at top)
- TL;DR: prefer cache-first for repeated prompts, batch when many concurrent small requests, streaming for interactive UIs. Provide fallback model & short circuit policy.

lina_cs: 1) Account health check before handoff
- Verify warm pool size >= projected TPS for first 2h.
- Ensure telemetry (latency, error-rate, tokens/s) is wired to their dashboard.
- Confirm key routes have tracing enabled.

lina_cs: 2) Caching guidance (customer-facing)
- Recommend prefix cache when >30% identical prompt heads. TTLs: 10m for highly dynamic sessions, 24h for stable system messages.
- Stale-while-revalidate pattern for UX: return cached + async refresh when possible.
- Storage: shared LRU with max-entry-size 1MB per key.

lina_cs: Sample cache config to share:
```yaml
route: /generate
cache:
  enabled: true
  type: prefix
  ttl_seconds: 600  # 10m
  stale_while_revalidate: true
  max_entries: 20000
```

lina_cs: 3) Batching guidance (customer-facing)
- Use batching for many small requests (<= 128 tokens). Target latency SLO 150-300ms.
- Recommend adaptive batch window: start 5ms, grow to 25ms under light load; 50-100ms under heavy load depending on SLA.
- Max batch size guidance: 64 for A100-class, 32 for smaller GPUs (if they're on Dedicated).

lina_cs: sample tune snippet for SDK (pseudocode):
```js
client.setBatching({ windowMs: 25, maxBatch: 64, maxWaitMs: 100 });
```

lina_cs: 4) Streaming guidance
- Use streaming for chat/assistant UIs. Recommend initial partial tokens flush at 50ms intervals or after sentence boundary.
- If streaming fails, fall back to non-streaming single-response endpoint with a short retry (1 immediate, 1 after 250ms).

lina_cs: 5) Fallback & graceful degradation
- Route fallback order: primary -> quantized variant -> smaller context model.
- Circuit breaker: open after 5xx rate > 3% for 1m, cooldown 30s.

lina_cs: 6) Customer-facing checklist to hand to engineers
- Confirm API keys and scopes
- Run the perf script (link) and capture baseline tokens/s
- Enable per-route telemetry and set alert at 2x baseline latency
- Agree on TTL and batch window policy in the kickoff call

lina_cs: 7) Feedback capture (how CS will monitor)
- Weekly snapshot for first 14 days: 99th percentile latency, error spikes, cache hit rate, batch sizes.
- Quick NPS pulse at day 7 for developer experience.

lina_cs: 8) Talking points for the customer call (short)
- "We’ll start conservative: small warm pool + cache-first. If you need lower latency we’ll increase warm pool and tighten batch windows."
- "We’ll watch cache hit-rate and adjust TTLs — changes are low-risk and reversible."

anna_cs: LGTM — love the TL;DR. Two small asks: call out who owns telemetry on our side and add a quick sample curl to verify cache behavior.

lina_cs: Good call. I’ll add owner + curl snippet.

marcus_sre: Note on cache size: for multi-tenant Dedicated, advise tenants to cap per-tenant entries or risk memory thrash. Also suggest soft-eviction on OOM pressure.

kevin_eng: For batching: remind them to send a small "probe" traffic pattern during business hours so we can tune adaptive window. Also add sample circuit-breaker config we use internally:
```json
{"failure_threshold_pct":3, "evaluation_window_ms":60000, "open_duration_ms":30000}
```

anna_cs: Added curl snippet suggestion:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/generate?route=/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt": "hello", "cache_key": "greeting_v1"}' -i
```

lina_cs: Updated owner tag: telemetry owner = "platform-observability" (cc @marcus_sre). I trimmed doc to one page for the customer.

deploy-bot: Reminder: docs repo updated at commit 7b4f3c — shared link in #docs.

marcus_sre: One more ops note: recommend enabling server-side sampling of traces at 10% for the trial to avoid cost blowup.

kevin_eng: And put a short rollback plan in the call notes: if latencies spike >2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes, revert TTL to 0 and reduce batch window to 5ms.

anna_cs: Perfect. I’ll take this into the call and post a short follow-up thread with the customer's selected TTLs and batch policy. :thumbsup:

lina_cs: Thanks all — will export as single-page PDF for the customer and attach in the kickoff invite."
